solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Community recall something yellow from space spinning with ends inverted (4,6)

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so FROM EM is read backwards
the two ends of the assembled string are turned upside down, trading places

blocks.note: the yolk of an egg is yellow
FROM + EM (a printer's space), turned round
YOLKMEMORF with its first and last letters swapped

annotation.surface: Someone remembers a yellow object that came tumbling in from outer space.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' is not a link word here but part of the fodder, and an em is a printer's unit of space. The final swap of the outer letters turns YOLK into FOLK and MORF into MORY.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrase-for-phrase match: the community is the folk, and what it collectively recalls of its past is its memory.

entries.clue: Out of shape with change of heart (4)

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and here those two middle letters change order

blocks.note: form = shape
the middle OR becomes RO

annotation.surface: Something has lost its figure and its feelings at once.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of shape' reads as one phrase, but 'Out of' is the definition and 'shape' the word to be altered.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for marking a source: made out of wood, made from wood.

entries.clue: Naked thug invades new Italian republic (9)

indicators.note: a naked word is stripped of its outer layer, its first and last letters
an invader pushes inside, so HU goes into the other piece
the letters of ITALIAN are made new, rearranged

blocks.note: THUG without its first and last letters
ITALIAN rearranged, with room after its third letter

annotation.surface: A thug with no clothes on bursts into a newly founded Italian state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' pulls towards Italy, but 'new' makes it fodder; the stripped thug then lands in the middle of a Baltic nation instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Baltic state has been an independent republic since 1990.

entries.clue: Nick is in plan favouring power over one in charge (14)

indicators.note: IS is placed in the next piece, MAP
in a down clue one piece sits over, above, the next, so P comes before RIATE
one in charge: the I is placed in the word for charge

blocks.note: a map = a plan
goes inside MAP, after the M
pro = in favour of
P = power in physics
I = one
a rate is a charge; I goes in after the R

annotation.surface: A man called Nick features in a scheme that prefers raw power to whoever is in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is the British slang verb, to steal. 'One in charge' suggests a boss; it is I inside RATE.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: in Britain to nick something is to steal it, and misappropriating funds is stealing them.

entries.clue: Knight doctor for keeping calm given final twist? (7)

indicators.note: MD holds the next word, keeping it inside
the final letters of ORDER get twisted round, ER becoming RE

blocks.note: MD = Doctor of Medicine
ORDER (calm, as when order is restored) with its last two letters swapped

annotation.surface: A knight asks a doctor for something to keep him calm, with a sting in the tail.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the end of ORDER is twisted, not the whole word, and the result sits inside MD.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the traitor of Arthurian legend who fought King Arthur was a knight of the Round Table.

entries.clue: Celebrate first person being enrolled seemingly (7)

indicators.note: to be enrolled is to be put on a list, a roster, so I goes into that word

blocks.note: I is the first person singular
the list someone enrolled is put on; I goes in after RO

annotation.surface: Someone throws a party on becoming the first person to sign up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enrolled' does double duty: it names the roster and puts I inside it, which is why the setter adds 'seemingly'.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym with colour: it means to celebrate in a noisy, rowdy way.

entries.clue: Twilight beginning to diffuse Welsh river (4)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of 'diffuse'
the Usk flows through south Wales

annotation.surface: Evening light starts to spread over a river in Wales.
annotation.walkthrough: The Usk is a river in south-east Wales, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the fading light after sunset goes by either word.

entries.clue: Flag carried in universal European custom (5)

indicators.note: something carried in is held inside its carriers, here U and E

blocks.note: U = universal, the film certificate
to flag = to droop, sag
E = European

annotation.surface: A flag is borne in a procession according to a Europe-wide tradition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb, to tire or droop.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: established practice, as in 'by long usage' or 'by long custom'.

entries.clue: Station sign somehow breaks 1000 times (5,5)

indicators.note: the letters of SIGN are arranged somehow, any old way
the rearranged letters break into the other pieces, splitting them apart

blocks.note: K = a thousand, as in £10K
SIGN rearranged
the times sign × is a cross

annotation.surface: A station sign gets smashed, a thousand times over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' is the multiplication sign, ×, and the rearranged SIGN breaks in between K and CROSS.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: it is one of London's main-line railway terminals.

entries.clue: County re-elects Irish eccentric earl (14)

indicators.note: something eccentric behaves oddly, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters
E = earl, the abbreviation

annotation.surface: A county council returns an Irish peer with odd habits to office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' sits between the two parts of the fodder but applies to both.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: it is a county of the English Midlands, with Leicester as its county town.

entries.clue: Primarily, officer aiming to ease Scott? (5)

definitions.text: Primarily, officer aiming to ease Scott?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Officer Aiming To Ease Scott

annotation.surface: A question about the motive of an officer on Scott's expedition.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the description: the five initials spell the man it describes.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes Captain Lawrence Oates, who walked out into the Antarctic blizzard to spare Scott's party the burden of his illness.

entries.clue: Make a fuss [of] dry hair, barely entering shower (5,4)

indicators.note: a bare word is stripped of its covering, its outer letters
the dry and hair pieces enter the shower word, going inside it

blocks.note: a shower of rain; the other pieces go in before its N
sec = dry, of wine
HAIR without its outer letters

annotation.surface: Someone complains about having to dry their hair after barely stepping into the shower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry' and 'shower' belong together in the bathroom but have nothing to do with each other here: SEC is the wine term.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to raise Cain, after the biblical troublemaker, is to cause a noisy commotion.

entries.clue: Labels on estates, maybe huge spades and hearts (6,8)

blocks.note: a bumper crop is a huge one
S = spades, the card suit
ticker is slang for heart

annotation.surface: The labels on landed estates list huge numbers of spades and hearts, like a card game.
annotation.walkthrough: An estate is a British estate car (a station wagon), not a country property. 'Spades and hearts' looks like two card suits; only spades is.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'maybe': estate cars are one kind of vehicle that carries such labels on the back.

entries.clue: Kind of charming desire to occupy toilet a lot (10)

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so the desire word goes inside the toilet

blocks.note: WC = water closet
an itch to do something is a desire; it sits between W and C
a raft of = a lot of

annotation.surface: Someone who is rather charming keeps wanting to spend a long time in the loo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind of charming' reads as an adjective, 'quite charming'; it is a noun phrase, a kind of charming in the sense of casting charms.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense of charming is working charms, spells, and the magic art of doing so is one kind of it.

entries.clue: Italian gentleman, duke, wanting introduction set aside (7)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the introduction of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: SIGNORE, Italian for sir or gentleman, less its S
D = duke

annotation.surface: An Italian nobleman is shoved to one side without being introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: The first letter goes from SIGNORE-D taken as a whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past participle: a complaint set aside has been disregarded.

entries.clue: King perhaps takes good man [for] some kind of thief (7)

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so RULER takes ST inside

blocks.note: a king is one kind of ruler
ST = saint, a good man; it goes in after RU

annotation.surface: A monarch recruits a virtuous man to catch some sort of thief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good man' for ST is a standard shortcut: a saint.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: one who steals cattle or horses is a particular kind of thief.

entries.clue: Clumsily running lines going round houses (9)

indicators.note: to house something is to give it room inside, so LOOPING houses LL

blocks.note: looping = going round
L = line, doubled; it goes in after LO

annotation.surface: An awkward runner takes lines that circle round a housing estate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like buildings to be circled; it is the verb that puts LL inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: to lollop is to move along with clumsy, bounding strides.

entries.clue: Fellow Conservative more willing to shun Republican (7)

indicators.note: to shun is to keep away from, so HAPPIER keeps away its R

blocks.note: C = Conservative
happier = more willing, as in happy to help
R = Republican, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A Tory colleague is keener than ever to avoid a Republican.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' looks like a colleague of the Conservative; it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a jaunty old British word for a chap, a fellow.

entries.clue: Wandering blackleg stuck in Morecambe? (7)

indicators.note: something stuck in is lodged inside, so RAT is lodged inside the Morecambe word

blocks.note: Eric Morecambe, the British comedian
a blackleg (strikebreaker) is a rat; it goes in after ER

annotation.surface: A strikebreaker is stranded in the seaside town of Morecambe.
annotation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort; the question mark points to Eric Morecambe, of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym from the Latin root 'errare', to wander: something erratic strays from a steady course.

entries.clue: ISP charging lead joining termini of line ending in famous Scottish town (7)

indicators.note: to charge something is to fill or load it, so EE is loaded into the lead symbol
termini are end points, so take the two end letters of 'line'
take the last letter of 'famous'

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
EE is a British internet and phone provider; it goes between P and B
surface glue: the pieces simply join on in order
first and last letters of LINE
last letter of FAMOUS

annotation.surface: An internet provider bills for a cable connecting the two ends of a line, in a well-known Scottish town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charging lead' looks like a phone cable; lead is the metal, PB, and 'charging' means filling.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: it is a small market town in the Scottish Borders, on the Tweed.

entries.clue: Cover involving dreadful Rolling Stone (7)

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap in, so TOP takes DIRE inside
something rolling turns over, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: a top is a cover; DIRE goes in after TO
dire = dreadful

annotation.surface: A cover version features an awful member of the Rolling Stones.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' is the band, but 'Rolling' turns TO-DIRE-P round and 'Stone' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this green gem, a form of olivine, is a precious stone.

entries.clue: Barristers once condemned French photographer (7-7)

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked, fit to be broken up, so the letters are broken and reset

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Lawyers once had a French photographer convicted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' is fodder, not a time word; without it the letters fall short.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Henri, pioneer of street photography and co-founder of Magnum, was French.

entries.clue: Hernia regularly blocking both sides of an organ (5)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every second letter
to block a gap is to fill it, so ENA sits between the two sides
the two sides are right and left

blocks.note: R = right, L = left, split to take the middle
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of HERNIA

annotation.surface: A hernia is pressing on both sides of some bodily organ.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Both sides of an organ' looks like a single phrase; it splits into 'both sides' (R and L) and the definition 'of an organ'.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the kidneys, so 'of an organ' is a definition by category.

entries.clue: Beginning of something new after loadsamoney raised (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue a raised word is read from bottom to top
the letter for new is placed after the raised word, following it

blocks.note: a wad of notes is loads of money, read upwards
N = new

annotation.surface: A fresh start comes after the flashy money is raised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of something' looks like a first-letter instruction for S; it is the definition. Loadsamoney was a 1980s British comic character, a byword for flaunted cash.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: the first light of day stands for the start of anything, as in the dawn of an era.

entries.clue: Italian Madam admitting state returned [for] added notes (9)

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so DONNA lets the state word in
something returned goes back the way it came, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: donna is Italian for lady, madam; the state goes in after D
état is French for state

annotation.surface: An Italian lady confesses the state of her comeback, jotting in the margins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returned' seems to belong to 'state' alone, but it turns D-ETAT-ONNA round as a whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb in the past tense: whoever wrote comments in a text's margins added notes to it.

entries.clue: Periodically, rival business plugs holiday destination (5)

indicators.note: at regular periods, so take every second letter
to plug a hole is to fill it, so the business word fills the gap between I and A

blocks.note: the 2nd and 4th letters of RIVAL
biz = business, informal; it goes between the two letters

annotation.surface: Now and then a competing firm advertises a holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' reads as advertises, which suits the business surface; it means fills a hole.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Balearic island is famous as a party and beach resort.

entries.clue: Segment of scintillating glacial deposit (4)

indicators.note: a segment is a piece cut out, so the answer is cut from inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters run from the fourth to the seventh of the word

annotation.surface: A glittering slice of glacier rubble.
annotation.walkthrough: The geologists' sense is the one needed, not the cash drawer or the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical sense: geologists use the word for the unsorted clay and stones a glacier leaves behind.

entries.clue: Arm broken — cast urgent (7-3)

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are broken up and reset

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A broken arm urgently needs a plaster cast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a trip to casualty; 'Arm' is a weapon and 'cast' only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a shotgun is a firearm, and arms are weapons.
